summary: Salmon fillets laid among sweet potato, peppers and onion for the last ten minutes of a vegetable roast. Leave the skin on and roast the fillets whole; no turning or pan-frying is needed.

ingredients.note: Fish allergen. The source leaves the skin on and sets it against the pan.

ingredients.item: Sweet potato, cut into 1 cm cubes
Bell peppers, cut into pieces about 2 cm by 2 cm
Small red onions, peeled and cut into wedges

ingredients.note: For the vegetables. The source drizzles a little extra over the salmon and marks that as optional.

ingredients.quantity: The source seasons to taste and gives no weight.

method.instruction: Heat the oven to 220°C conventional, or 200°C fan (gas mark 7). Both figures are stated by the source; neither is a conversion made here.
Spread the sweet potato, peppers and onion over a very large roasting pan in a single layer.
Drizzle over the 2 tablespoons of oil, scatter the thyme, season, and turn everything to coat before spreading it flat again.
Take the pan out, stir the vegetables and spread them flat, then settle the four fillets among them with the skin against the pan. Drizzle with a little oil if you are using it, and season.

Roast for a further 10 minutes, then measure the thickest part of each fillet. The recipe source leaves doneness to preference; Health Canada gives a 70°C internal endpoint for fish. The source specifies a 130 g fillet but no thickness, so the cooking time may vary. Continue cooking and recheck if needed.

yield_note: Serves 4, as stated by the source. Source times: 5 minutes preparation and 25 minutes cooking. The source gives no resting time, and none is invented here.

provenance_note: Recipe facts paraphrased from Eb Gargano's page at Easy Peasy Foodie, accessed 2026-09-14; the safety threshold is Health Canada's. The recipe source leaves fish doneness to preference and gives no measured endpoint. The 70°C endpoint comes from Health Canada. No fillet thickness is stated by the source; only the 130 g weight is. The source writes tablespoons without stating a millilitre value, so no spoon size is asserted here.

caveats: Health Canada gives a 70°C internal endpoint for fish. Some diners prefer less-cooked salmon; that preference does not establish that the fish has reached this safety endpoint.
Raw fish and its packaging contaminate surfaces. Wash hands, board and knife after handling, and do not rest cooked fillets where the raw ones sat.
Allergen: fish. The dish contains no gluten or dairy as written, but check any seasoning you add.
